sonnet.problem: The blank asks the baker to guess the wording of the line ("does not satisfy"). Nothing earlier lets a baker reason to "satisfy" over "last" or "grow".
sonnet.rule: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

sonnet.problem: The blank asks the baker to guess a word in verse 4 ("a witness to the ___"). No earlier card sets up a reasoned pick between nations, priests and prophets. This tests wording, not meaning.
sonnet.rule: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

sonnet.problem: The blank asks for the verb "prosper" in verse 11. Nothing earlier lets a baker reason it out over "rest" or "wait". It is a wording guess.
sonnet.rule: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

sonnet.problem: The card says "The message closes" with verse 12, but verse 13 and more cards follow. It also tells a prediction ("You will indeed go out…") as people "heading out" now, and it names the addressed "you" as "the people", which the text doesn't say. Card 12 repeats this with "As the people go out".
sonnet.rule: A prediction stays a prediction... / Leave open what the text leaves open. Who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

sonnet.problem: The joke calls back to "the day the angel made me new" without saying who the angel is or the drawer it called him out of. In his backstory the angel was a messenger; the Most High makes things new.
sonnet.rule: Bakers may not know anything about his story. Anything from his backstory, like the drawer, the Millers, the shiny new stamper or the angel, is said in the line itself, like "the angel who called me out of that drawer."
